items_missed: Never restated the hourly rate, the "pricing is super simple" opener, or the what's-included rundown (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, tools) — the whole pricing section was skipped in favor of just confirming the online quote
No "no hidden fees" pitch and no explicit no-deposit-required statement
Never asked directly whether Shannon needed packing services (she volunteered she'd pre-pack herself, unprompted)
No typical time range or mover/truck count was given for the job
Variables affecting the estimate (stairs, the 100-ft walk, the credenza) were gathered as facts but never explicitly tied back to how they affect price or time
"Take a carload yourself" tip was missing from the prep/Save Your Ass speech, and there was no "does that make sense?" sense-check after either the clock explanation or the prep speech
Used the customer's name (Shannon) only once, in the opening greeting — never again for the rest of the 9-minute call
No Ecobox/box-service referral despite a lengthy discussion of the ~20-30 boxes needed
Insurance explanation covered No Worries Damage Coverage well but never mentioned the state-mandated per-pound liability baseline for comparison
top_strength: Bri thoroughly re-confirmed every logistical detail of the online quote (addresses, square footage, stairs, the TV and credenza, boxes, and a tricky gate/parking access situation) and proactively worked around the customer's cat-related scheduling concern, keeping Shannon relaxed and chatty for the whole call.
coaching_note: Because this was a confirmation call for an existing online quote, Bri skipped nearly the entire pricing/differentiator pitch (hourly rate, what's included, On-Time Guarantee, no hidden fees) and should still work those in briefly plus use the customer's name more than once — both reinforce value and rapport even on a details-confirmation call.
phone_presence_notes: Bri stayed warm and attentive throughout, apologizing when she misspoke about the arrival window and empathizing with the customer's cat concerns, which kept Shannon comfortable and talkative for the full call.
